"He was not wicked, no more so than any young boy" Which is to say yes, little boys are very much little sociopaths. I understand why the Czar did what he did, but my god was that anger misplaced.

item.content:encoded:
if i may…

The overall idea is that 914 might not actually be working right. What is currently contained is the guts, the most core systems of the overall machine. It's like a car engine, you can do a hell of a lot to it, even tear out bits and damage it, and it'll still turn over and work, just not "right". The ages of neglect, damage, and general wear and tear and caused damage both major and minor. It works, but perhaps not as well, or even in the way, that it was intended.

It was meant to be a toy, of sorts, to provide wonders and such. The refining aspects are possibly one subset of the overall function, but as they are the most core, they are what has survived all these years. In the past, when it was still in good shape, it may have been capable of much, much more.

Then again, your perception may be completely different, but that's my overall thrust.

item.content:encoded:
I never really thought much about the backstory of 914 before. It never even occurred to me to - I always vaguely figured that there was probably no explanation ever in mind for it, or that if there was, it was some throwaway paragraph or two, nothing remotely as interesting as the SCP itself. After all, the 'logic' of 914, the way it seems to almost make sense, to always have a weird sort of rightness to it, and yet never to quite become understandable, was rightly fascinating, and the origin had no bearing on that in my mind.

I was oh so wrong. This is just a masterpiece. It's taken what was already my favorite SCP on this site and raised it to a new level entirely. That ending line, just… Damn. Goddamn.

I'll be looking at other SCPs I never really considered on depth in a whole new light after this.

Not that this needs it, nor that this hasn't all been said well before my late comment, but take my +1 with all the enthusiasm I can muster.

item.content:encoded: Indeed, there are no bad concepts, only bad execution. People like George Lucas fail in their attempts at expanding on previously established tales and/or characters not because such an expansion is an intrinsically bad idea, but because the way he went about doing so was hampered by poor decisions that lessened the impact of the original concepts while not being satisfying in terms of being something new. Gears is not like that.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
See Gears, here's the thing. With most of us, we write something vague, and then if we reveal what we're hinting at the readers are disappointed. I'd argue that the disappointment stems not from the loss of mystery, but from the author's explanation being somehow… less than whatever vague thing we imagined the truth might be. Too simple, too formulaic, whatever- the truth cheapens it.

And then there's you. You give us 914, and then years later you make a reveal, and and somehow it's more than most of us imagined. You give us a closer look at 106 in Treats, and we're left with an image of 106 more disturbing than the photo ever was. Off the top of my head I'm not sure if you've done anything else that I'd construe as "veil pulling", but even these two are a hell of a precedent: both have made the originals richer.

I suppose the point I'm trying to make is this: you're purported to have this enormous untold meta-backstory linking virtually everything you've written for the site. Should you ever reveal all of it? Absolutely not. But if tales like this are what we get when you gamble with your comfort zone, then let it ride sir- you'll have to go a hell of a lot farther than this before you disappoint.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This one definitely deserves it. It is an amazing piece of writing that you should feel proud of.

I feel like a lot of stories that try to expand on the background of established SCPs (actually just established anythings [I'm looking at you George Lucas!]) tend to diminish the mystery/horror/wonder of the thing (the more you know about something, the less frightening or amazing it tends to be).

This does the exact opposite. This is terrifying, but at the same time has this sense of the mystical, and the sadness and madness and pathos and just everything works together so well. I think it touches a deeper place in me than the original article managed to, and for that, you get my +1. (Technically gave it to you a while ago, but I just realized I never posted to tell you how absolutely brilliant this story is. So now I have.)

item.content:encoded:
Thanks a bunch, i'm glad you dig it so much. Complexity breeds madness, i've found. Even more so when it's poorly understood. As for the style, I try to be aware of the "when" in a story. It's a old, old device, so I tried to hit a older, slightly more "lofty" style, which I think i hit enough to not stress over.

I'm always torn with these kinds of stories. I have these big, weird backstories for all my entries, but I have to walk the line of not wrecking the weirdness…I'm glad that, for most, this helps rather then hurts.
